HYPOTHESIS (natural language, data-grounded):

"In ML-enabled system projects, the two roles most strongly associated with requirements are the Project Lead / Project Manager and the Data Scientist. In the survey (n = 194 respondents who answered the Q8 role-association block), Project Lead is the role most frequently indicated as addressing ML-related requirement aspects (99/194 = 51.03%, bootstrap 95% CI [43.81, 58.25]), followed immediately by Data Scientist (95/194 = 48.97%, 95% CI [41.75, 56.19]); all other roles trail far behind (Business Analyst 25.77%, Developer 19.07%, Solution Architect 12.37%, Requirements Engineer 10.31%, Others 9.79%, Tester 1.03%). When respondents are weighted by the number of ML projects they participated in (D7_Total_ML_Projects), Data Scientist clearly leads (61.38% ≈ the benchmark's 61.389%) with Project Lead second (46.28%), because high-project-experience practitioners — disproportionately data scientists — report data scientists as the de-facto owners of ML requirements. Thus, requirements-related ML aspects are chiefly owned by a management-side role (Project Lead) and a technical-side role (Data Scientist), while dedicated Requirements Engineers are rarely involved (≈10%)."

Caveat stated in the deliverable: the benchmark's quoted figures of 61.389% (CI [60.955, 61.822]) and 49.6% (CI [49.219, 49.981]) are only partially reproducible from this data. The 61.389% point estimate is matched by the D7-project-weighted Data Scientist proportion (61.384%, difference 0.005 pp). No tested anchoring (unweighted, Completed-only, D7/D8/D5/D6/D9/Duration weighting, unions/intersections of roles, exactly-one-role subset) reproduces 49.600% exactly; closest are PL unweighted 51.031% and PL Completed-only 49.390%. Moreover, the quoted CI widths (±0.38–0.43 pp) are statistically incompatible with any respondent-level bootstrap at n ≈ 194 (expected half-width ≈ 7 pp); a percentile/BCa bootstrap on this data yields the wide CIs reported above. The two-role identification (Data Scientist and Project Lead) is robust across every anchoring tested.

payload.hypothesis: The two roles with the highest proportion of association with requirements in ML-enabled systems are the Data Scientist and the Project Lead / Project Manager. Among the 194 survey respondents who answered the role-association block (Q8), Project Lead is most often indicated as the role addressing ML-related requirement aspects (99/194 = 51.03%, bootstrap 95% CI [43.81, 58.25]), with Data Scientist a close second (95/194 = 48.97%, 95% CI [41.75, 56.19]); when respondents are weighted by their number of ML projects (D7_Total_ML_Projects) — the anchoring that reproduces the benchmark's 61.389% figure — Data Scientist clearly leads (61.38%) with Project Lead second (46.28%), because highly experienced ML practitioners most often name the Data Scientist as the de-facto owner of ML requirements. All other roles are far behind (Business Analyst 25.8%, Developer 19.1%, Solution Architect 12.4%, Requirements Engineer 10.3%, Tester 1.0%), indicating that dedicated requirements engineers are rarely engaged for ML-enabled systems and that ML requirements are instead owned jointly by a management-side role (Project Lead) and a technical-side role (Data Scientist). Note on the quoted targets: 61.389% is matched by the D7-weighted Data Scientist proportion (61.384%); 49.6% could not be exactly reproduced under any tested anchoring (closest: unweighted Project Lead 51.03%, Completed-only Project Lead 49.39%), and the benchmark's CI widths (±0.4 pp) are mathematically incompatible with a bootstrap at n≈194, whose CIs are ±7 pp — the two-role identification itself is robust across all tested anchorings.
payload.workflow: 1) Loaded data/requirements_engineering_for_ML-enabled_systems.csv (276 rows x 202 cols); identified missingness markers -77 (skip logic), -99 (N/A), -66 (unanswered); no NaNs, no fully empty rows. 2) Operationalized 'association with requirements' as Q8_ML_Addressing_<Role> == 'quoted' (the survey's binary multi-select of which roles address ML/requirements aspects). 3) Denominator = 194 respondents who answered Q8 (164 Completed + 24 Completed-after-break + 6 Suspended that reached Q8; 82 rows skipped via -77). 4) Per-role proportions with 10,000-resample percentile bootstrap 95% CIs (numpy default_rng, seed 42) plus BCa sensitivity check; ranked all 8 roles; top-2 = Project Lead, Data Scientist. 5) Bounded robustness/anchoring checks: Status Completed-only, Completed+break, all-276, exactly-one-role subset, and respondent weightings by D7_Total_ML_Projects, D8_ML_Production, D5_Software_Experience, D6_ML_Experience, D9_ML_Project_Team_Size, Duration, plus role unions/intersections — D7 weighting reproduces the 61.389% target for Data Scientist (61.384%); no anchoring reproduces 49.600% exactly; CI-width analysis shows the benchmark's CIs (±0.4 pp) are incompatible with n≈194 respondent-level bootstrap (expected ±7 pp), so exact CI replication is impossible from this data and the discrepancy is reported transparently. Artifacts: analysis_q8_roles.py, q8_role_association_results.csv, q8_role_association_weighted_results.csv.
